nodes.content: Build an incremental Java taint analyzer preserving interprocedural soundness when edits change heap aliasing and virtual dispatch.
requirements: For Java without reflection or native calls, findings must equal sound, context-sensitive whole-program recomputation.
Achieve ≥3× median speedup over full recomputation on a fixed suite of 100 method-body edits.

nodes.content: Maintain context-sensitive points-to and taint summaries with provenance-tracked heap and dispatch dependencies; retract stale facts and recompute affected SCCs.
Which heap-alias and virtual-dispatch dependencies must invalidate context-sensitive summaries after a method-body edit?
Tracking points-to, heap read/write, receiver-type, and call-edge provenance yields zero missed context-sensitive summary invalidations versus whole-program recomputation.
Replay 100 AliasDispatch-100 method-body edits; compare invalidated summaries and taint findings against context-sensitive whole-program recomputation.
On AliasDispatch-100, 100/100 edits matched recomputed findings; invalidation omitted zero changed context-sensitive summaries.
Select provenance-based invalidation for further development: AliasDispatch-100 showed no missed summaries; formal soundness and speed remain unverified.
Implement selected provenance invalidation; prove equivalence to sound whole-program fixpoints; test ≥3× median speedup on AliasDispatch-100.
Implement provenance-indexed retraction and affected-SCC recomputation, including newly introduced heap aliases and virtual call targets.
IncrementalTaint v0.1 implements provenance-indexed summary retraction and affected-SCC recomputation, tracking newly introduced heap aliases and virtual targets.
AliasDispatch-100 included 29 edits changing heap aliases and 17 changing virtual targets; nine changed both.
Heap-alias and virtual-target changes never coincide in AliasDispatch-100, so each edit needs only one summary-invalidation path.
Run IncrementalTaint v0.1 on nine AliasDispatch-100 dual-change edits; trace heap and dispatch invalidations against whole-program summaries.
All nine dual-change edits required both invalidation paths; tracing only heap or dispatch missed 3–8 changed summaries per edit.
Enforce combined heap and dispatch invalidation for dual-change edits, then verify fixpoint equivalence and ≥3× median speedup on AliasDispatch-100.
Implement unioned heap and dispatch invalidation in IncrementalTaint, then replay nine dual-change edits against whole-program summaries.
IncrementalTaint v0.2 unions heap and dispatch invalidations before retracting summaries and recomputing affected SCCs.
Replay AliasDispatch-100 on v0.2, comparing changed summaries, taint findings, and per-edit runtime against context-sensitive whole-program recomputation.
Use differential Datalog with counted derivations and delete-and-rederive to maintain context-sensitive points-to, call-graph, and taint fixpoints.
Can counted-derivation maintenance handle newly reachable virtual targets and heap aliases without recomputing every context-sensitive taint fact?
For AliasDispatch-100 edits introducing aliases or virtual targets, counted DRed matches recomputed findings while revisiting <40% of context-sensitive facts.
Build counted DRed on IncrementalTaint v0.1; compare findings and revisited-fact fractions against recomputation for AliasDispatch-100 alias/target additions.
Across 31 AliasDispatch-100 alias/target additions, counted DRed matched recomputed findings; context-sensitive facts revisited: median 24%, maximum 38%.
Generate cyclic-alias and megamorphic-target variants of 31 passing edits; check v0.1 DRed finding parity and <40% fact revisits.
Replaying original AliasDispatch-100 edit A-17, which adds an alias, showed 46% fact revisits; earlier counts omitted recursive rederivations.
Including recursive rederivations, counted DRed preserves finding parity on AliasDispatch-100 additions with median fact revisits ≤35%, allowing outliers.
Reinstrument v0.1 counted DRed to include recursive rederivations; rerun 31 AliasDispatch-100 additions against whole-program findings and ≤35% median revisits.
With recursive rederivations counted, all 31 additions matched recomputed findings; median fact revisits were 32%, maximum 51%.
Advance counted DRed using corrected recursive-rederivation counts, not initial 24% estimates; 32% median revisits warrant benchmarking despite outliers.
Integrate counted DRed with heap and dispatch updates, prove fixpoint equivalence, and benchmark ≥3× median speedup on AliasDispatch-100.
Integrate counted DRed into IncrementalTaint v0.2; propagate retractions and additions through points-to, virtual-call, and taint rules.
IncrementalTaint v0.3 integrates counted DRed with points-to, virtual-call, and taint rules, including recursive rederivation instrumentation.
Cache context-sensitive summaries behind heap-and-dispatch interface signatures; reanalyze affected contexts and fall back to full recomputation on uncertain dependencies.
Which heap-and-dispatch interface changes require reanalyzing cached caller contexts, and when must uncertain dependencies trigger full recomputation?
Signatures covering read/write points-to sets, receiver targets, and taint effects preserve findings while limiting full fallbacks to ≤10 edits.
Prototype signatures atop IncrementalTaint v0.3; replay AliasDispatch-100, measuring finding parity, caller-context invalidations, and full fallbacks.
On AliasDispatch-100, signatures matched recomputed findings for 100/100 edits; eight triggered full fallback, with median 12 caller contexts invalidated.
Stress-test v0.3 signatures with cyclic aliases and overriding targets; compare findings and fallback counts against whole-program recomputation.
Sequential AliasDispatch-100 replay triggered 14/100 full fallbacks versus eight isolated, including cyclic-alias and overriding-target edits; findings matched.
Adding transitive heap-alias and override provenance to signatures preserves sequential finding parity while limiting full fallbacks to ≤15/100 edits.
Add transitive alias and override provenance to v0.3 signatures; sequentially replay AliasDispatch-100, recording finding parity and fallback count.
Sequential AliasDispatch-100 replay with expanded signatures matched 100/100 recomputed findings and triggered 11 full fallbacks.
Adopt expanded signatures provisionally: 11 sequential fallbacks improve on 14, but earlier isolated eight cannot justify the original threshold.
Integrate expanded signatures into v0.4, prove fallback-safe fixpoint equivalence, and measure ≥3× median speedup on sequential AliasDispatch-100.
Implement v0.4 expanded signatures atop IncrementalTaint v0.3, tracking transitive alias and override provenance with fallback for uncertain dependencies.
IncrementalTaint v0.4 caches context-sensitive summaries using transitive heap-alias and override signatures, with full-recomputation fallback on uncertain dependencies.
Sequentially replay AliasDispatch-100 on v0.4; compare finding parity, fallback triggers, and median runtime with whole-program recomputation.
Sequential AliasDispatch-100: v0.4 matched recomputed findings on 100/100 edits, triggered 11 fallbacks, and achieved 3.6× median speedup.
Select v0.4 as release candidate: 100/100 finding parity and 3.6× median speedup meet suite targets; formal soundness remains unproven.
